sources.entry: Pinpoint by gowtham012 - Local MCP server, Claude Code hooks and a Chrome extension for marking up a running app: clicking an element (or one in the iOS Simulator) and typing a change delivers the comment to Claude Code with the selector, DOM path, computed styles, component chain, source-file hint and a cropped screenshot.

summary.one_liner: Pinpoint is a local MCP server, Claude Code hook set and browser extension (plus iOS Simulator and Android emulator pickers) that lets you click or box-select a running app's UI and send the annotated element, with context, to a coding agent.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a bridge on 127.0.0.1:7331 that receives annotations from a Chromium or Firefox extension, the iOS Simulator picker, or the Android emulator picker. For web pages each note includes a CSS selector, DOM path, computed styles, rendered text, bounding box, framework component chain, a source file:line hint where the dev build exposes it, and a cropped element screenshot. Agents receive notes via Claude Code hooks, MCP tools (get_pending_annotations, recheck_annotation, resolve_annotation, reply_annotation, wait_for_annotation and others), or a watch loop. Agents can reply with questions, and users can accept or reopen finished notes, with Before/After crops. Native iOS notes come from the accessibility tree via Maestro, and Android notes from the adb view tree.
use_cases: Marking up UI changes on a local dev site for a coding agent
Pointing an agent at a specific button or card instead of describing it
Sending bug reproduction steps with page errors to Claude Code
Annotating iOS Simulator or Android emulator screens for an agent
Giving Cursor or Codex a visual, element-level change request
Reviewing agent changes with Accept or Not quite replies in the browser
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd pinpoint/bridge && npm install
Load extension/ unpacked at chrome://extensions with Developer mode on (setup prints the path)
claude mcp add pinpoint -s user -- npx -y pinpoint-bridge mcp
node cli.js --project ~/code/my-app  (start the bridge and leave it running)
Restart Claude Code once so it picks up the MCP server and hooks
stack: Chromium extension (Manifest, also Firefox 140+ and Safari wrapper)
Model Context Protocol (MCP), stdio and Streamable HTTP
notable: Sends a selector, computed styles, component chain, source hint and cropped screenshot with each note, so the agent does not have to guess which control was meant
Works with native iOS Simulator and Android emulator screens, not just browser pages
Supports behaviour notes and multi-step recording of a bug with network and console errors attached
Agent and user can converse on a note: agent can ask questions, and the user can reopen a resolved note
Multiple agents share one queue, with wait_for_annotation assigning each note to one waiting agent
caveats: Native iOS and Android paths have no source-file hint, no computed styles and no recheck_annotation tool; iOS first load can take about 10 seconds or more

Safari lacks MAIN-world content scripts, so component chain, source hint and page errors are unavailable there; Chrome Web Store and Edge listings were pending at the time of the README, so unpacked loading is needed
Windows needs manual handling for the native host (install-native-host is macOS and Linux only), and the bridge only runs on local development hosts by default
keywords: tell my ai what to change on the page
annotate a web page for an ai
